title: Weather Watch

beats.narrativeText: The expedition's weather station still functions intermittently, and Atlas asks the learner to restart its observations.
Today's weather must be compared with archived expedition records to see what changes over time.
The learner records today's observations and measures (or estimates) the temperature.
The learner creates simple charts to compare historical and current weather data.
The learner must identify patterns emerging from the comparison between old and new data.
The patterns begin to explain some of the earlier expedition's decisions.
The learner reflects on how today's observations connect to events from long ago.
The learner's new evidence becomes part of the expedition archive, and weather becomes an ongoing factor to track.

activities.title: Record Observations
activities.storyContext: The weather station still functions intermittently, and Atlas asks the learner to restart its observations.
activities.instructions: Record today's weather conditions — sky, wind and any other details you notice.
activities.output: A weather observation entry in the Explorer Journal.

activities.title: Measure Temperature
activities.storyContext: Accurate readings will let today's weather be compared with the expedition's archived records.
activities.instructions: Measure today's temperature if a thermometer is available, or estimate it carefully if not.
activities.output: A recorded or estimated temperature reading.

activities.title: Create Simple Charts
activities.storyContext: A chart will make it easier to compare weather data over time.
activities.instructions: Create a simple chart to record your weather observations.

activities.title: Compare Historical and Current Data
activities.storyContext: Patterns begin emerging that may explain some earlier expedition decisions.
activities.instructions: Compare today's chart with the expedition's archived weather records.
activities.output: Notes on how today's weather compares with the archived records.

activities.title: Predict Tomorrow's Weather
activities.storyContext: Explorers use evidence to make predictions, not guesses.
activities.instructions: Use your collected evidence to predict what tomorrow's weather will be like, and explain your reasoning.
activities.output: A weather prediction with supporting reasoning.

activities.title: How Meteorologists Make Forecasts
activities.storyContext: Predicting weather is a real scientific discipline.
activities.instructions: Find out how meteorologists make weather forecasts.
activities.output: None required — this is an open investigation.

prompts: What pattern did you notice when comparing today's weather with the archived records?

discussionPoints: What pattern did you notice in the weather data?
Why might weather have affected the expedition's decisions?
parentGuide.preparation: A thermometer is useful if available, but estimating is acceptable.
parentGuide.assessment: Look for accurately recorded observations and a chart that makes a pattern easy to see.

completionCriteria: Weather observations recorded, charts created, and historical data compared with current data.
